title: Impossible to conjugate an unknown quantum state via a unitary evolution
abstract: The no-cloning theorem, the no-deleting theorem, the no-hiding theorem, the no-flip theorem, and the no-broadcasting play a crucial role in quantum mechanics and quantum information. In this paper, we propose the no-conjugating theorem which states that it is impossible to conjugate an unknown arbitrary quantum state via a universal physical device or linear/unitary operation.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes and proves the 'no-conjugating theorem,' showing that an unknown quantum state cannot be transformed into its complex conjugate state using any unitary operation. The proof uses algebraic methods applied to the qubit system, extending the body of known no-go theorems in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the 'no-conjugating theorem,' which asserts that it is impossible to transform an unknown arbitrary quantum state into its complex conjugate state using any universal unitary evolution.
main_result: The no-conjugating theorem is established, demonstrating that no universal unitary operator can map an arbitrary unknown state $|\psiangle$ to its conjugate state $|\psi^*angle$.
method: The proof relies on algebraic manipulation of the unitary transformation equations derived from assuming the existence of such an operator, leading to contradictions.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on a single unknown arbitrary quantum state (a qubit) $|\psiangle = \alpha|0angle +  eta|1angle$ and its unitary evolution $U$.
key_observables: The unknown state $|\psiangle$, its conjugate $|\psi^*angle$, and the resulting state $|\psi'angle$ after unitary evolution.
important_parameters: The coefficients $\alpha$ and $ eta$ defining the unknown state, and the structure of the $2 	imes 2$ unitary matrix $U$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a universal unitary operator $U$ capable of performing the conjugation, which is then shown to be impossible.

paper_structure: The paper builds upon established no-cloning and no-broadcasting theorems, first proving conditions under which conjugation is possible (Theorem 1), then establishing the general impossibility (Theorem 2), and finally proving the no-conjugating theorem by setting the target state to the conjugate state $|\psi^*angle$.
why_interesting: This work extends the fundamental limitations of quantum operations (like no-cloning) by proving a new impossibility theorem regarding state conjugation, which has implications for quantum measurement and state reconstruction.
